As of my last update, André Jean René Lacrampe was a Roman Catholic clergyman from France, most notably serving as a bishop in the Catholic Church. Born on September 2, 1941, in Bordères-sur-l'Échez, France, he was ordained as a priest on September 22, 1966. He was appointed Bishop of Ajaccio in France on December 22, 1995, and served there until he was appointed as the Archbishop of Besançon on May 10, 2003.

Throughout his career, André Lacrampe was known for his pastoral sensitivity and dedication to the needs of his diocese. His service in various pastoral and clerical capacities reflected his deep commitment to the Church's mission and to addressing the spiritual and social needs of the communities he served.

He held the archbishopric position in Besançon until his resignation on March 3, 2013, usually a reflection of a bishop or archbishop reaching retirement age, which for Catholic bishops is typically set at 75. After his resignation, he likely assumed the title of Archbishop Emeritus of Besançon. 

There isn't widely available detailed information about his accomplishments or specific initiatives during his time as a bishop and archbishop, but like many of his peers, his work would have involved a mix of spiritual leadership, administrative responsibilities, public representation of the Church, and addressing various ecclesiastical and community issues. 

To get more up-to-date or detailed information, it would be advisable to look at recent publications or official Catholic Church announcements that may provide a deeper insight into his later life or any additional roles he may have undertaken after his resignation as archbishop.
